name: MonarchTypeToConfirmInput
title: TypeToConfirmInput
summary: A text field in which the person types a name, such as "acme-site", to confirm an irreversible action.
whenToUse: Before deleting or transferring something that cannot be restored, when a plain confirmation dialog is not enough.
whenNotToUse: For an action that can be undone, use an undo snackbar (MonarchSnackbarHost) instead. For ordinary text input use MonarchTextField.
api: @Composable fun MonarchTypeToConfirmInput(phrase: String, value: String, onValueChange: (String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, label: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, showMismatch: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true, onMatchChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, mismatchMessage: String? = null, matchAnnouncement: String? = null, mismatchAnnouncement: String? = null, keyboardActions: KeyboardActions = KeyboardActions.Default, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
object MonarchTypeToConfirmInputDefaults { val KeyboardOptions: KeyboardOptions; fun matches(text: String, phrase: String): Boolean }

options.name: phrase
options.description: The exact text the person must type, usually the record's own name.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the new text. Paste is allowed.

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label. By default "Type “phrase” to confirm" (monarch_typetoconfirminput_label).

options.name: helperText
options.description: Guidance under the field, for example what is about to be deleted.

options.name: showMismatch
options.description: Shows the error while the text does not match. Set it after a submit attempt.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the person can edit the field.

options.name: onMatchChange
options.description: Called each time the match state flips, not for the first state.

options.name: mismatchMessage
options.description: Replaces the built-in "The text does not match."

options.name: matchAnnouncement
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Text matches" announcement. An empty string is silence.

options.name: mismatchAnnouncement
options.description: Announced when the text stops matching. Nothing by default.

options.name: keyboardActions
options.description: What happens when the person triggers the IME action.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the focus and press interactions of the field.

states.name: not matching
states.description: A plain text field. No error unless showMismatch is set.

states.name: mismatch shown
states.description: The text field's error state: the danger border, the error message and the error semantics.

states.name: matching
states.description: A plain text field; the match is announced and reported, not drawn.

appearance: The same field as MonarchTextField: the input border role, the focus ring role when focused, the danger strong role for the border and message in the error state, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web shows the phrase in a monospaced face inside the label; MonarchTextField takes a plain string label, so the default label puts the phrase in quotation marks, as iOS does. Matching is the web's rule: case-sensitive, ignoring surrounding white space. The web's static phraseMatches is MonarchTypeToConfirmInputDefaults.matches, since a Kotlin function cannot carry a static member. The web announces through a role=status region; Android uses a polite live region on a node that is always present. The value is hoisted (value and onValueChange), so there is no uncontrolled defaultValue.
accessibility: The field is read as a text field whose label names the phrase.
"Text matches" is announced through a polite live region when the typed text starts to match.
The mismatch error is text and the error semantics property, set only when showMismatch is true.
The error never shows while typing unless the app sets showMismatch.
Autocorrection and capitalisation are off, so the keyboard does not change the typed name.
The field is a Material 3 text field with its 48dp minimum height; text grows with the font size setting.
edgeCases: Spaces and line breaks around the typed text and around the phrase are ignored; spaces inside are not.
An empty phrase matches empty text.
onMatchChange is not called for the first state, only for changes.
The component does not disable any button; use onMatchChange or MonarchTypeToConfirmInputDefaults.matches for that.

examples.title: Basic
examples.template:
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput(
    phrase = {{phrase}},
    value = typed,
    onValueChange = { typed = it },
    helperText = {{description}},
)
examples.code:
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput(
    phrase = "acme-site",
    value = typed,
    onValueChange = { typed = it },
    helperText = "The site, its pages and its form entries are deleted.",
)

examples.title: Error after a submit attempt
examples.setup:
var typed by remember { mutableStateOf("acme") }
val triedToDelete = true
examples.code:
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput(
    phrase = "acme-site",
    value = typed,
    onValueChange = { typed = it },
    showMismatch = triedToDelete,
)
